items.title: Seeing the Sun's far side in flux transport models
items.summary: New in ApJS: a probabilistic framework that brings helioseismic far-side active regions into the AFT model. Near-side-only runs miss 10-20% of the Sun's total magnetic flux.

items.title: 265 years of solar surface magnetism, rebuilt
items.summary: New in ApJ: daily magnetic maps of the whole Sun for Solar Cycles 1 to 24 (1755 to 2020), made with our Synthetic Active Region Generator and the AFT model. The maps are public.

items.title: Using 100-year-old data to help predict future solar cycle activity
items.summary: SwRI press release on our historical reconstruction work, picked up by EurekAlert! and SpaceDaily.

items.title: A near-real-time model of the solar corona, in Science
items.summary: Co-author on a data-assimilative coronal model that keeps itself current with new magnetic-field observations.

items.title: autotabpy released on Zenodo
items.summary: The Python version of AutoTAB, our automatic tracker for bipolar magnetic regions.

items.title: Invited talk at Space Climate 9, Nagoya
items.summary: A window into the past: simulating the Sun's historical photospheric magnetic field with AFT.

items.title: When will the Sun's poles flip in Cycle 25?
items.summary: Our ApJL forecast with the AFT model: north around August 2024, south around February 2025.
